data.caption: Feel Like Yourself Again
data.copy:
I rear ended a woman's car at a red light. I never touched the brake.

Not because I was on my phone. Not because I was drunk. Not because I fell asleep.

Because my brain simply didn't register that I needed to stop.

The light turned red. The car in front of me stopped. And I just... kept going. Like I was watching it happen from outside my body. Like the signal went from my eyes to my brain and got lost somewhere in between.

The airbag hit me so hard it left a bruise across my chest that lasted three weeks. I sat there in the driver's seat with my ears ringing, and one thought repeating over and over.

What is wrong with me.

Because the truth is, the accident didn't come out of nowhere.

I'd been losing myself for months. Maybe longer.

Walking into the kitchen and standing there with the refrigerator open, staring at shelves, trying to remember what I came in for. Then walking back to the couch and remembering two minutes later. Then forgetting again before I could get up.

Reading the same paragraph four times and still not absorbing a single word. My eyes would move across the page but nothing was landing. Like my brain had a coating on it that words just slid off of.

Sitting on a work call and realizing someone just asked me a direct question and I had no idea what the last three minutes of the conversation were about. Nodding, saying "Can you repeat that?" again. The third time this week.

Putting my keys in the freezer. Leaving the stove on overnight. Calling my daughter by my sister's name twice in the same dinner. She laughed the first time. The second time she looked at me like she was scared.

Driving past my exit on the highway. Not once. Three times in two weeks. Routes I've driven for 15 years.

Trying to do basic math at the grocery store and pulling out my phone calculator for 12 plus 7.

data.caption: VAGUSNERV!!! Die Lösung für Arbeitsstress👆
data.copy:
Der wahre Grund, warum Entspannung nicht funktioniert 🧠🚫

Mein Körper kam von der Arbeit heim – aber mein Gehirn nicht. Bis ich um 2 Uhr nachts die wahre Ursache verstand.
Irgendwann zwischen 22:00 und 23:30 Uhr sehe ich das Muster.
Jeden verdammten Abend das gleiche. Laptop zu, ich fahre nach Hause. Körper im Auto, aber der Kopf? Der sitzt noch im 14:30-Uhr-Meeting fest. Die E-Mail von meinem Chef um 17:45 Uhr geistert mir immer noch durch den Schädel.
Meine Frau sitzt auf der Couch, will mir vom Tag erzählen.
Ich nicke, aber innen bin ich noch bei der Präsentation. Sie merkt es. Ich merke, dass sie merkt. Das ist das Schlimmste daran.
Gegen 23:00 Uhr liege ich im Bett. Augen zu. Aber mein Körper – Nacken hart wie Beton, Schultern bis zu den Ohren hochgezogen – sagt meinem Gehirn: "Achtung, Alarm, noch nicht sicher."
Ich kann nicht einschlafen. Oder ich schlafe ein und wache um 3 Uhr auf, weil meine Gedanken wieder rasen.
Morgens wache ich auf und fühle mich völlig ausgelaugt. Obwohl ich 7 Stunden "geschlafen" habe.
Das geht seit Monaten so.

Die verzweifelte Suche:
Ich versuche alles.
Atemübungen. Diese 4-7-8-Atemtechnik, überall empfohlen. Funktioniert 2 Minuten, dann bin ich wieder beim Gedanken: "Habe ich vergessen, auf die Slack-Nachricht zu antworten?"
Ein Freund schwört auf Meditation. Ich lade eine App herunter. Sitze 10 Minuten in der Stille und mein Hirn dreht noch schneller. Das ist nutzlos.
Mein Arzt schlägt vor: "Weniger Stress."
Habe ich versucht. Das ist kein Life-Hack, das ist eine dumme Antwort.
Hot Yoga. Ein Wärmekissen auf der Couch. Sogar eine Massagepistole, die meine Schulter brutal durchschüttelt. Alles bringt kurzzeitig etwas, dann ist der Nacken wieder fest.
Und dann – 2 Uhr morgens, ich liege wieder wach – googele ich etwas anderes. Nicht "wie entspannt man sich", sondern: "Warum kann ich nicht abschalten?"
Das ist der Moment, der alles ändert.

Die Erkenntnis:
Ich lese über etwas, das ich nicht erwartet hat…

data.caption: How to Kick the Habit by Tricking Your Brain ☝️
data.copy:
It was 11:47 PM when I found my mom collapsed on the bathroom floor, gasping for air like she was drowning on dry land.

I'm Tyler, a 22-year-old engineering student from Florida. All my life, I'd been watching my mom slowly kill herself with cigarettes, but that night in March changed everything.

Mom had been a pack-a-day smoker for 18 years. Started in college, just like I was now. "Just socially," she used to say. "I can quit anytime."

We'd tried everything. Nicotine patches that gave her rashes. Gum that made her nauseous. Vapes that she claimed "just weren't the same." Cold turkey attempts that lasted maybe 36 hours before the shaking and irritability became unbearable.

But that Tuesday night was different.

I'd come home late from the engineering lab to find her wheezing on the couch, her face slightly blue-tinged in the TV light.

"Mom, you okay?" I asked, already knowing the answer.

She waved me off, trying to speak but only managing a rattling cough that sounded like gravel in a blender.

By 11 PM, the coughing hadn't stopped. By 11:30, she was struggling to walk to the bathroom. By 11:47, I was calling 911 while she clutched her chest on the cold tile floor.

The ER doctor's words still echo in my mind: "Stage 2 lung cancer. We caught it early enough to treat, but she needs to quit smoking immediately. Not reduce. Not switch to vaping. Quit completely."

Mom survived. The treatments were brutal – chemotherapy that left her exhausted, radiation that burned her throat, surgery that removed part of her left lung.

But here's the part that broke me: Even facing death, even after everything we'd been through, I'd still catch her sneaking outside, desperately trying to light up with shaking hands.

"I can't help it, Tyler," she sobbed one night after I found her with a pack she'd hidden. "My brain won't stop screaming for it. It's not the nicotine anymore – it's the action, the ritual, the feeling. My hands don't know what to do. My mouth feels empty. I …

keyword.description: Free-text search string (lowercased server-side). Use for product names, brands, hooks, domains — not for category/niche (use niches).
keyword.allowed_values: Any string; empty = no text filter.

searchkeyword.description: Which ad field keyword searches. NOT a niche/category selector.
searchkeyword.allowed_values: All, landingurl, pagename, adtext, productname. Default All when keyword is set.

countries.description: Ad target countries (where the ad runs — wlads.countries). Not store HQ.
countries.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated ISO2: US, GB, DK, NL, BE, IE, NO, SE, FR, DE, IT, CA, NZ, AU, BR, AT, CH, ES, FI, PL, PT, GR, TR, AE, SA, QA, KW, BH, OM, JO, IL, LB, IQ, EG.

storebasedin.description: Store Based In (dashboard storebasedin → store_traffic.shop_origin_country). Use for Mexico/Colombia/Chile/etc. store HQ.
storebasedin.allowed_values: Comma-separated ISO2 including MX, CO, CL, AR, PE and other Explore Shops Based In markets.

See allowed_niches in response for code→label map. Fashion/clothing = CG.

website.description: Detected store/checkout technology on the landing page (dashboard Website filter).
website.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated codes: SH, TP, BU, LS, CC, SL, TA, GG, FU, CS, LP, FO, SI, GP, XS, YC, HY, DI, MS, SB, PP, WC, TT, TW, PI, GO, SC, FB, MG, WP, SQ, PS, GM, KV, CO, HJ, WX, AR, BC, MC. SH=Shopify, WC=WooCommerce, CS=Clickfunnels. See allowed_technologies in response.

excludeLanguages.allowed_values: Comma-separated: en, nl, de, no, fr, sv, da, it, pt, es, fi, pl, tr, ar, he.

apps.description: Shopify apps detected on the store.
apps.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated app names/ids from dashboard Apps filter. See allowed_apps in response.

excludeApps.description: Exclude stores using these Shopify apps.
excludeApps.allowed_values: Comma-separated app names/ids. See allowed_apps in response.

themes.description: Shopify theme name on the store (exact match).
themes.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated exact theme names from dashboard Themes filter (discover via GET /api/themes).

scaling.allowed_values: rising, stable, declining, nodownscaling, upscaling, downscaling.

mediafilter.allowed_values: videos, images, carousel, dco. Omit/All = all formats.

pagetypefilter.allowed_values: products, collections, funnels, nofunnels. Empty/All = all types.

adscorefilter.description: WinningHunter ad score tier (Established / Has Potential / Unestablished).
adscorefilter.allowed_values: winning (Established), scaling (Has Potential), testing (Unestablished). Requires matching account tier.

lowimpressions.description: Hide ads with very low impressions.

rankgrowthfilter.description: Within-brand ad rank momentum vs historic rank_history.

maxadspend.description: Maximum EU ad spend in window.
maxadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. 999999 treated as no upper cap server-side.

adspendtimeframe.description: Rolling window ad spend is summed over (NOT a calendar month filter).

minreach.description: Minimum EU reach/views total in reachtimeframe window.
minreach.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

reachtimeframe.description: Rolling window reach is summed over.

mintraffic.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

minproductsonstore.description: Minimum published products on the Shopify store.

minprice.description: Minimum product price on landing page.

mincopylength.description: Minimum ad primary text character length.

minvideolength.description: Minimum video duration in seconds (use with mediafilter=videos).

mindays.description: Minimum days the ad has been running.
mindays.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

from.description: Ad launch date lower bound (Meta started field — when ad began running, NOT scrape date).
from.allowed_values: YYYY-MM-DD. Requires to on same range.

to.notes: To isolate ads running in a calendar month: ad_created_to=last day of month AND fromlastseen=first day of month.

product_from.description: Shopify product creation date lower bound.

pagefrom.description: Facebook page creation date lower bound.

activestatus.description: Legacy dashboard param (no longer applied to ES queries).
activestatus.allowed_values: Ignored — use adstatus or last_seen_from/to instead.

adstatus.description: Dashboard Status filter — recently seen vs stale ads.
adstatus.allowed_values: active (lastSeen or updated_at within last 4 days), inactive (neither field within last 4 days), All/empty (no status filter).
adstatus.notes: find_winning_products forces active. Same as dashboard Status = Active.

sorting.allowed_values: relevance, datefound, mostrecent, lastseen, adspend, longestrunning, reach, adsetamount, consistency, monthlyvisits, monthlytraffic, monthlyrevenue, pageactiveads, toprank, mostsaved. Aliases: rank/top_ad/best_ranked→toprank (asc = best rank first, desc = worst rank first). ad_started→mostrecent. monthly_visits→monthlyvisits. monthly_traffic→monthlytraffic.

page.description: Pagination page index (informational). Deep pagination requires scroll from the previous response — incrementing page alone does not advance the result set.
page.allowed_values: MCP uses 1-based page (1=first page); echoed value is 0-based internal page sent to API.

scroll.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Empty/omit on the first request; pass the response scroll value on the next request with the same filters to fetch more ads. Required to download beyond the first page (especially sort_by=lastseen).
scroll.allowed_values: Opaque string from previous response; empty string or omit for first page. Stop when scroll is null/absent or data is shorter than a full page.

mcp_pagination.hint: Pass scroll_next as scroll on the next call with the same filters to continue. Do not rely on page alone.
